blocks.text: AHIJAH THE SHILONITE, THE PROPHET OF SHILOH · UNITED KINGDOM
Ahijah. Tore a new garment into twelve pieces, and later sent Jeroboam's wife home with heavy tidings.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophet
ERA
United kingdom c. 1050–930 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Solomon · Jeroboam I · Rehoboam
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
He acted the word out: he took hold of the new garment, tore it in twelve pieces and told Jeroboam to take ten.
THE CALL
How the word came
He acted the word out: he took hold of the new garment, tore it in twelve pieces and told Jeroboam to take ten. 1 Kings 11:29–31
When Jeroboam's wife came disguised, “the LORD said unto Ahijah, Behold, the wife of Jeroboam cometh”, though Ahijah “could not see; for his eyes were set by reason of his age”. 1 Kings 14:4–5
Chronicles names “the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite” as a record of Solomon's acts. 2 Chronicles 9:29
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before three kings
KING OF ALL ISRAEL
Solomon
KING OF ISRAEL
Jeroboam I
“Take thee ten pieces: for thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel, Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee:”
1 Kings 11:31 (KJV) →

Rehoboam

HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textKings last shows Ahijah old and unable to see; it does not tell of his death. 1 Kings 14:4
TRADITION SAYS

Rabbinic tradition identified him with Ahiah son of Ahitub, the priest at Shiloh in Saul's time (1 Samuel 14:3), and counted him among seven long-lived saints whose lives span the history of mankind; on this reckoning “Ahijah lived over six hundred years”. 1 Samuel 14:3 [41] Who says so: The Midrash and the Talmud (Baba Batra 121b), as reported in the Jewish Encyclopedia, rabbinic writings; reported 1901
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Ahijah's own
C. F. Keil (1872); John Gill (1748–1763); the Pulpit Commentary (1880–1897)
Keil: “he rent the new garment, that is to say, his own, not Jeroboam's”; Gill: “not Jeroboam, but the prophet”. 1 Kings 11:29–30 [64][29][86]
Jeroboam's
H. Ewald, as reported by Keil and the Pulpit Commentary
Ewald took “he had clad himself” to mean Jeroboam, and saw in the new garment his “splendid robe of office”. 1 Kings 11:29 [64][86]

Every passage

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture gives no father for Ahijah and does not tell how he became a prophet.
Kings does not give the name of Jeroboam's wife.
“The prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite” (2 Chronicles 9:29) is not among the books of the Bible.
